items.title: Jon Jang interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 17, 2003 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Billy Taylor, I’ve collaborated with him at the Asia Society of New York in 1995

ctx.x: I guess I was just wondering, the work you do, to me, requires a fairly sophisticated listening audience. And I worry that we still have that as time goes by.

Well your concern is something that I have seriously considered. And that’s why I think I do have to have multiple ways to, like the other question to survive. And I don’t think I could just survive just doing that kind of music. But that doesn’t mean that I’m going to — I mean there’s other ways to see Jon Jang because I’m very versatile. And one of the weaknesses I’ve had over the years is because I’ve had to create all these ambitious projects with such great artists that my voice as a pianist has been…
Would you feel comfortable for instance trying to book a trio gig at, is it Yoshi’s in Oakland? Is that the jazz club there?
